text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
VIETNAM NEWS

-- Vietnam's National Assembly chairman Nong Duc Manh concluded a three-day visit to Thailand in Bangkok on Saturday after a trip to an overseas Vietnamese community in Udonthani province, about 300 km northeast of the Thai capital.

-- Six road building companies from the United States, Germany and Taiwan have expressed interest in taking part in the construction of a 72-km Hanoi ring road. Among the companies showing an interest in the $700 million project were Consortium og United States American Consulting Engineers, another American group called B.O.T. Consortium and a Berlin-based firm CBF.IPROP.

-- Over 200 representatives from firms under direct management of the Trade Ministry and the provincial Trade Services met in Ho Chi Minh City to study market and trade issues. Trade Minister Le Van Triet outlined trade goals and forecast a 20-30 percent rise in exports and a 24-percent increase in imports by 2000. BUSINESS

-- The Asian Commercial Joint Stock Bank (ACB) in Ho Chi Minh City will become the second domestic commercial joint stock bank to have public equity after receiving permission to issue stock. The bank will sell 30 percent of its stock to foreign individuals and organisations as part of a capital increase.

-- The State Treasury will issue two-year bonds with an annual coupon of 12 percent to individuals from Tuesday. The minimum value of each bond, which are not available to companies, agencies and mass organisations, will be 100,000 dong ($9.09).

-- Japan's Lotte co Ltd and Nisso Iwai Corp will form a joint venture in Vietnam to set up a hamburger chain. According to the Nihon Keizai Shimbun, the $600,000 venture will set up its first Lotteria restaurant in Ho Chi Minh City next May.

-- A range of imports from the European Union will enjoy a new preferential tax base. Vietnam and the EU signed their first framework agreement on lower tax rates for textiles and clothing in December 1992, resulting in a two-percent reduction. - - - -
LE COURRIER DU VIETNAM

-- Jean-Louis Roy, Secretary General of the Francophone Agency, visited Hanoi to discuss preparations for the Francophone summit in November 1997 in the Vietnamese capital. The agency signed an agreement on projects costing about $3 million.

-- Daewoo Director General Joo Sung kim told a news conference that the group's investment in Vietnam will reach $3 billion in 2000. Daewoo is the leading foreign investor in Vietnam, ploughing $725 million into 14 joint venture projects since 1991.
-- Twenty firms have already expressed an interest in bidding for an over $28-million contract to upgrade a 30-km stretch of Highway 1 running south of Hanoi. Bidding will start in January. - - - -
NHAN DAN
-- The VietsovPetro joint-venture has so far exploited 40 million tonnes of crude oil.
-- In preparation for the flood season, 25 billion dong ($2.3 million) worth of preferential loans has been accorded to Mekong Delta farmers to build and reinforce their houses.
-- A three-month English-language course for high-ranking goverment officials, part of a bilateral cooperation programme between Vietnam and Australia, ended on Saturday. - - - -
QUAN DOI NHAN DAN

-- Vietnam's trade deficit was $3.25 billion in the first eight months of this year with exports of $4.35 billion and imports of $7.6 billion. However, researchers said a deficit generated by imports of machinery, equipment and materials was not a worry because jobs would be created from export-oriented production.

-- A study on nuclear applications has been completed and evaluated by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Environment. The project was aimed at selecting and expanding nuclear applications in scientific, social and economic fields.
-- Construction of a state-of-the-art lighhouse has been completed in Tran island off Quang Ninh province). - - - -
HA NOI MOI
-- Reinforcement works around Hanoi's West Lake started on Sunday. The first stage, involving investment of 1.7 billion dong ($154,545) is expected to be completed by December.
